transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what made me come in today is that I just keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody. I feel like a fake in my apprenticeship, honestly. Like I'm letting my family and the newer apprentices down over... I don't know, just stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from. But I just can't shake the feeling.
When these thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do something repeatedly to reduce your distress?

No, not really. I don't do anything over and over, if that's what you mean. I mostly just... sit there and feel bad about it. I don't really have any specific habits or routines to make the feeling go away, it just kind of stays stuck in my head.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been... about nine months, I'd say. This depressed stretch has just kind of been with me for a while now. It definitely got a lot harder to hide once my classes and the apprenticeship work started slipping, but yeah, around nine months.
During this nine-month period, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you usually like?

Yeah, I definitely have. Lately, I can just walk right past my sketchbook and not even pick up a pencil. I've been skipping volleyball, too, and... I just ignore the texts from my volunteer group. I don't really feel much of anything about it, which is weird, because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself. Now I just don't have the interest.
Over the past nine months, have you felt sad, down, or depressed on most days?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or down most days. It's more just... what I was saying before, about not caring. I don't really feel much of anything, so I'm not sitting around crying or feeling super depressed in that way. It's just kind of a blank feeling.
Did this loss of interest begin after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
No, not really. I can't think of anything specific that happened. It just kind of started on its own, I guess. There wasn't any big change or stressful event that set it off.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different areas of your life, and having difficulty controlling the worry?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have normal stress with work and stuff, but... I don't find myself worrying excessively about a bunch of different things. And I definitely don't feel like I can't control it. Honestly, it's kind of the opposite right now—I'm almost not caring enough to worry about much.
Have you had thoughts of dying or suicide during this nine-month period?

No, I don't have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I don't know, sometimes when I'm driving home from work, or just lying awake at night, I get these thoughts. Like, it just crosses my mind that it would be a lot easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. But I wouldn't actually do anything.
During this nine-month period, have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy?

No, not really. I mean, my job is pretty physical, so I definitely get regular tired after a long shift. But I haven't noticed any unusual drop in my energy or anything like that. Just the normal amount of tired.
How has your sleep been during this nine-month period?

It's been pretty messed up, honestly. For a while there, I was getting by on maybe three or four hours a night, and I'd still show up totally wired for my job and my classes. But now... it's like I either can't fall asleep at all, or I wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just feel like I never even rested.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually energized or unusually irritable compared with your usual self?

Yeah, actually. Um... there were a few weeks where I felt almost too good. Just like Miami was mine, you know? But at the same time... I don't know, every little comment from a coworker who slowed me down on a job made me snap way harder than I normally would.

{"intent":"Determine whether the unusually energized and irritable period caused marked impairment or other features inconsistent with hypomania.","question":"During that unusually energized period, did it cause serious problems in your work, relationships, or daily functioning?")}

Yeah, it kind of did. Um... my instructors and my foreman have had to chase me down a lot about unfinished sketches and just, you know, doing slower work than usual. I'm honestly pretty scared that I'm close to damaging my apprenticeship. I've worked really hard to get on track for this certification, so having them on my case about my performance is definitely a problem.
During that unusually energized period, did you lose touch with reality, such as hearing or seeing things that others could not?
No, nothing like that. Um... I definitely didn't hear or see anything that wasn't actually there. I was just really sped up and on edge, but I always knew what was real.
Did you ever need to be hospitalized because of that unusually energized or irritable period?

No, I didn't. Um... I never had to go to the hospital for it or anything like that. It was definitely causing those issues with my apprenticeship, but it never got bad enough that I needed to be admitted anywhere.
During that period, did your thoughts feel unusually fast or difficult to keep up with?

Yeah, they really did. Um, my head would just jump around constantly. Like, I'd go from thinking about pipe layouts for work, to coming up with a whole business plan, to texting my classmates, to figuring out how to fix my mom's bathroom... all at the exact same time. I just couldn't slow my brain down enough to actually pick one thing and stick with it.
During that period, were you unusually driven to start or accomplish lots of projects or activities compared with your usual self?

Yeah, I definitely was. I just wanted to do everything. I signed myself up to help my classmates with their stuff, and I volunteered to do extra design sketches for work. I was even messaging old contacts trying to set up side projects. I just kept taking on more and more things, even though, looking back, part of me knew there weren't enough hours in the day to actually finish it all.
